chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on them both, said: We were told by Ahmad ibn Idris, and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marouzi, that he said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

Ghusl is a sa' of water, and Wudu is a mudd of water. The sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is five mudds, and a mudd is the weight of two hundred and eighty dirhams, and one dirham is the weight of six daniqs, and one daniq is six kernels, and one kernel is the weight of two barley seeds from the average seeds, not from their small ones nor from their large ones.

key_terms.دَوَانِيقَ: Daniqs (plural of daniq, a smaller unit of weight)
key_terms.مُدٌّ: Mudd (a unit of volume/weight, smaller than sa')

ai.seo_question: What is the exact amount of water required for Ghusl and Wudu according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* provides the foundational metrological definitions for ritual purity, linking the volumetric units of *sa'* and *mudd* to tangible weight standards like dirhams and barley seeds to ensure consistency in Shia jurisprudence. It reflects the scholarly tradition of anchoring abstract ritual requirements in precise, reproducible physical measurements, thereby preventing ambiguity in the performance of *Ghusl* and *Wudu*. This emphasis on quantifiable purity underscores the Shia focus on both the external correctness (*sihha*) and internal certainty (*yaqin*) of worship.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father and Muhammed bin Hasan, may Allah grant them both mercy, both said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, and Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammed bin Ahmad, from Ali bin Muhammed, from a man, from Sulayman bin Hafs al-Marouzi, that he said: Abu’l-Hasan, peace be upon him, said:

Ghusl [1] is (performed with) a ssaa’ of water, and Wudu is (performed with) a mudd of water. The ssaa’ of the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, is (consisting of) five mudds, and a mudd is the weight of two hundred and eighty dirhams, and one dirham is the weight of six dawaneeq  [2], and one daniq is (consisting of) six kernels, and one kernel is (consisting of) two seeds of barley, from the average seeds, not from their small ones nor big ones.
